answers: A channel receiver loops forever by design
The original tx is still alive, so the channel never closes
The receiver has to be declared mut to iterate
writing.exampleCaption: Ownership transfers with the message, so no lock is needed.
writing.explanation: An mpsc channel moves values from many producers to one consumer, and the move is what makes it safe — once sent, the sender no longer owns the value. The receiver iterates until every sender is dropped, so the loop ends on its own rather than needing a sentinel message.
writing.feedback: Every live sender keeps the channel open; drop the ones you do not use.
writing.question: Why might that loop never end?
writing.rule: The loop ends when the last sender is dropped.
writing.success: The receiving loop finishes without a sentinel value.
